thread:
incident-bot: SEV=P1 automatic alert — node-gpu-21 reported CUDA OOM while headroom metric shows ~11.8GiB free. Affected service: runtime-serving-prod-us-west-2. Alert: https://alerts.internal/realtime/2005432100 :rotating_light:

nayan (oncall): I'm taking this. pulling metrics and logs now. starting with `nvidia-smi -q` and runtime logs.

alex (runtime): noted. past incidents showed allocator reserves + KV-cache pin can make `available` appear high but actual allocatable contiguous chunk low. could be fragmentation or reserved blocks pinned by the runtime.

maria (infra): can you paste the OOM snippet? want to see exact allocate size and which GPU.

nayan (oncall): log snippet from runtime on node-gpu-21:
```
E runtime: cudaErrorOutOfMemory: out of memory when allocating 2251799813685248 bytes
Failed to allocate 2.1 GiB (requested) on GPU 0 -- total GPU mem: 40.0 GiB, headroom reported: 11.8 GiB
Stack: allocator::alloc() kvcache::pin_prefix() runtime::serve_request()
```

alex (runtime): that `headroom reported` is our telemetry view (free minus reserved summary). If reserved blocks are in a different pool (shadow reserve) or pinned to processes that crashed but left handles, the allocator can't reuse them. also fragmentation: many small free blocks but no contiguous 2.1GiB.

josh (sre): any immediate customer impact? I see increased 5xx rate on the prod-serving route.

leda (support): support-ticket #3589: 14 unique requests failed over last 3m, fallback to smaller model for ~80% of them, latency +200-400ms. notifying impacted customers - drafting pubmsg.

nayan (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) try live KV-cache eviction endpoint on node (non-disruptive) 2) if still OOM, restart runtime container on that node (disruptive) 3) if node flaps, cordon+drain and replace. executing step 1 now: `curl -X POST http://node-gpu-21.internal:3172/admin/evict_cache`

alex (runtime): evict_cache should free pinned entries. also add `--evict-prefix '*'` to be aggressive. do it on the specific pod instance.

nayan (oncall): evict returned 204, logs show ~3.6 GiB freed from KV cache. retrying request replay... still seeing one OOM for a large request (chat-with-long-context) then container crashed.

maria (infra): container crash -> kube shows CrashLoopBackOff. pulling `kubectl describe pod` and node dmesg.

nayan (oncall): `kubectl describe` shows container exited with SIGABRT. dmesg on node includes `Out of memory: Kill process 8421 (runtime) total-vm:...` weird because GPU-only OOM shouldn't trigger kernel OOM. maybe runtime hit host mem pressure due to pinned host-mapped buffers.

alex (runtime): runtime sometimes falls back to host staging buffers when GPU allocation fails; if those accumulate, host oom kills process. suggests allocator attempted fallback and got into partial cleanup race.

josh (sre): immediate action: restart runtime pod to restore serving. I'll do graceful restart of pod on node-gpu-21 now, with 30s drain to allow in-flight requests to failover.

nayan (oncall): executed `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-serving --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-gpu-21 --namespace=prod` on the pod instance. pod came back up in ~47s, readiness passed, traffic shifted back. Error rate trending down.

leda (support): update for customers: "We've observed transient errors affecting a small subset of requests in us-west-2 due to GPU memory allocation failures on a single node. We performed a targeted restart and cache eviction; service has recovered. No customer data was exposed. Follow-up postmortem will be shared." :white_check_mark:

maria (infra): we should cordon node-gpu-21 for deeper inspection. cordoning now and scheduling a dedicated repro job. `kubectl cordon node-gpu-21` done.

alex (runtime): follow-up steps I'm going to take: 1) enable verbose allocator trace for recent pod (capture alloc/free ranges) 2) add stronger pre-alloc contiguous-check path to avoid huge single-chunk requests if contiguity not available (serve smaller chunks) 3) PR to reduce shadow-reserve default from 6GiB -> 3GiB for the affected runtime image. will open PR and link.

nayan (oncall): handing off to maria for infra dive and to alex for runtime patching. I'm stepping out of rotation in 8m; @maria please escalate if node reproducible.

maria (infra): ack, taking over for deep-dive. first immediate checks: kernel nvlink logs, NVIDIA driver 525.x known fragmentation heuristics? capturing `pmon` snapshots and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free,memory.used --format=csv -l 1` for 2m.

josh (sre): I've opened incident ticket INC-2026 and linked this thread. tagging owners: @alex (runtime) for allocator patch, @maria (infra) for node repro, @sre oncall for follow-ups. Incident status: mitigated (service restored), customer impact: degraded for ~2m for small subset, next steps: postmortem + telemetry/alert tuning.

leda (support): sent customer notice. will post public status after PM review.

alex (runtime): quick note — existing metric "gpu_contiguous_free_bytes" is underreported because we sum free across subpools. I'll add a gauge for largest_contiguous_free_chunk to better catch this class of issue. PR created: https://git.internal/r/allocator/PR-421 (WIP).

maria (infra): found node-level reserved pages held by a stale process (PID 8421) even after container restart; looks like driver leaked a handle. raising driver ticket with vendor and capturing repro logs. creating GH issue: https://git.internal/r/infra/issue-992.

josh (sre): postmortem owners: alex (runtime), maria (infra), nayan (oncall) — please have initial draft in 48h. Also add follow-up: alert rule split for GPU headroom vs largest_contiguous_free_chunk so we don't get false sense of safety.

nayan (oncall): thanks team. I will add a short runbook note under /runbooks/gpu-oom-headroom-illusion.md for oncall steps (evict cache -> restart pod -> cordon node -> escalate to infra). handing the thread over to maria for further analysis.

maria (infra): taking it. I'll post findings and attach kernel logs in the issue. closing incident in this channel but leaving ticket open for follow-up. :lock:

incident-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) — summary: GPU OOM on node-gpu-21 despite reported headroom due to fragmentation + reserved/pinned allocations and a driver handle leak. Actions: eviction + pod restart mitigated; cordoned node for repro; patches and alert changes planned.
